LESSON: READING 12.4.1 PLAY: CHARACTERISATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words or expressions can you use to describe one’s character?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use the clues to describe the characters in a play
2. appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 12.4.1 PLAY: CHARACTERISATION
This lesson teaches Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation for Grade 9 ENGLISH.

STUDY STEPS
1. use the clues to describe the characters in a play
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation above.
2. Explain Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words or expressions can you use to describe one’s character?
2. Why is characterisation important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. use the clues to describe the characters in a play
2. appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
